title: The True Believer: Thoughts on the Nature of Mass Movements

contents: Part One: The Appeal of Mass Movements — Desire for Change; Desire for Substitutes; The Interchangeability of Mass Movements

Part Two: The Potential Converts — The Role of the Undesirables in Human Affairs; The Poor; Misfits; The Inordinately Selfish; The Ambitious Facing Unlimited Opportunities; Minorities; The Bored; The Sinners
Part Three: United Action and Self-Sacrifice — Prefatory; Factors Promoting Self-Sacrifice; Unifying Agents
Part Four: Beginning and End — Men of Words; The Fanatics; The Practical Men of Action; Good and Bad Mass Movements

audiences: Readers seeking a compact framework for why people join militant political, religious, or nationalist movements
Leaders, historians, and citizens who want diagnostic questions about recruitment, group unity, hatred, and movement life cycles
Readers comfortable treating forceful historical generalisations as hypotheses rather than scientific laws

sources.title: The True Believer: Thoughts on the Nature of Mass Movements
sources.author_or_publisher: Eric Hoffer; HarperCollins via Google Books
sources.supports: Searchable book passages, structure, numbered sections, core concepts, examples, and publication metadata.
sources.limitations: Preview access is uneven and does not expose every page in one continuous reading.

sources.title: The True Believer
sources.supports: 1951 publication, author, language, subject classification, editions, and preview availability.
sources.limitations: Edition metadata is community-maintained and some records merge Harper imprints; corroborated elsewhere.

sources.title: Review Essay: The True Believer
sources.author_or_publisher: Benjamin Buchholz; Military Review, US Army University Press
sources.supports: Current paperback metadata, four-part structure, appeal and convert arguments, movement substitution, and one practitioner application to violent extremism.
sources.limitations: Applies Hoffer to radical Islam from a US military perspective; the proposed applications are not validation of the general theory.

sources.title: Review of Eric Hoffer, The True Believer
sources.author_or_publisher: William J. MacKinnon; Philosophy of Science
sources.supports: Contemporary assessment of Hoffer's approach as armchair speculation from loosely controlled observation that can stimulate more rigorous theory and investigation.
sources.limitations: Short review of a later paperback edition; it does not test each proposition.

sources.title: That Other Big Book on Irrational Politics
sources.author_or_publisher: Andrew Seal; Society for U.S. Intellectual History
sources.supports: The book's postwar intellectual context, psychological portrait of the frustrated convert, broad method, and the qualifying importance of its final chapter.
sources.limitations: An interpretive intellectual-history essay, not an empirical test of mass-movement theory.

sources.title: Eric Hoffer's The True Believer and terrorism research
sources.author_or_publisher: Behavioral Sciences of Terrorism and Political Aggression
sources.supports: Later scholarly placement of Hoffer's framework within research on extremist belief, ideology, narrative, and political violence.
sources.limitations: Abstract and bibliographic access only; used for context, not detailed claims about findings.

sources.title: The True Believer: review
sources.supports: Detailed reconstruction of the fixed pool and interchangeability arguments and criticism of cherry-picked historical evidence.
sources.limitations: Long-form amateur review selected by a review competition, not peer-reviewed scholarship.

sources.title: The True Believer
sources.supports: Large reader aggregate and recurring praise for concision and relevance alongside criticism of unsupported assertion and overgeneralisation.
sources.limitations: Self-selected reviews, edition merging, and no control for expertise or completion.

sources.title: The Longshoreman Philosopher
sources.supports: Writing context, 1951 publication, intended backdrop of Hitler and Stalin, author career, and documented reception.
sources.limitations: The archive holds Hoffer's papers and presents his significance sympathetically.

workflow.coverage_notes: The searchable Google Books text and library preview were checked across all four parts and the 125-section progression, then triangulated with contemporary scholarship, later specialist analysis, and detailed independent and reader reviews. No uninterrupted lawful full text was available, so coverage remains sample-and-secondary.
